demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson reads acme's answers, pools and citations by the kit's own chunk ids, so point acme at its index for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors.

demos.heading: The two reports, row by row
demos.purpose: --report keeps, for each row, the request as it was sent (never a token or a header), the status, the outcome, the verdict, the reason, the first 300 characters of what was said, and the citations or passages. The comparison counts; the report lets you read. The cell checks that the two runs asked the same rows and that neither file holds a token, then prints each row that is not structural with both of its outcomes and the first words of each reply, or the detail rag-api gave when it refused.
